items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 2025-09-12, 2026-03-12, 2026-05-28). Current medications at the 2026-05-28 visit are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only; the only anticoagulants in the chart are inpatient dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban orders from January 2025, none of them current. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: CHF (I5040/I110 congestive heart failure, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure), hypertension (I10), age 80 (2 points), type 2 diabetes (E119/E11649), prior TIA/cerebral infarction (V1254, I69322/I69351) (2 points), vascular disease (old MI 412, coronary atherosclerosis I2510) and female sex. Guideline-indicated oral anticoagulation is absent; antiplatelet therapy alone is not an acceptable substitute.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25, continuously prescribed since at least 2023). Her most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, QRS 86 ms, QT 494 ms and Bazett QTc 534 ms (RR 0.86 s; per-lead tangent T offsets tightly clustered 478-510 ms). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review under the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. In addition, 40 mg daily exceeds the maximum recommended citalopram dose and she has hypothyroidism and prior acute kidney failure, all of which add to the torsade risk; dose reduction and a repeat ECG should be considered.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02, continuous since it was started at the 2024-05-14 cardiology visit). His most recent ECG in the chart, 108018814 of 2023-10-08, shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 486 ms and Bazett QTc 518 ms (RR 0.88 s; per-lead tangent T offsets clustered 473-500 ms). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list medication requires prescriber review. Note that the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same 2023-10-08 ECG as sinus rhythm, QT acceptable, which the measured QTc does not support. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2025-08-23) are normal, and no ECG has been repeated since starting the drug.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10. Because the start date is before 2026-03-01, the 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (The ECG itself showed QTc 527 ms, which is handled as a separate QT_SAFETY item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start predates 2026-03-01, so the original 2025-09-01 memo window of 30 days applies (the 2026-03-01 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day window), giving a due date of 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - within the 30-day window, so completed. The ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc 425 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on or after 2026-03-01, the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded 2026-03-07, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc 373 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo applies: ECG required within 14 days, due 2026-04-24. No ECG was obtained inside that window - the only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not satisfied within the required time and is overdue as of the evaluation date. (That late ECG showed sinus rhythm 69 bpm, QTc 378 ms, so no QT safety issue, but the monitoring requirement itself was missed.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the drug was started - and no outside ECG is referenced. The due date has passed, so this monitoring requirement is overdue.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 for her psychotic disorder. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained yet (last ECGs 2025-03-08/09), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked to ensure the ECG is done by 2026-09-29.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart for the patient at all, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the 14-day window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained, would satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives; the report should be chased and the QTc reviewed.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was met.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I480) coded at the 2025-03-14 admission, during which she also had a cardioembolic cerebral infarction (I6340 cerebral infarction due to embolism, I69354 residual hemiplegia). She has never been anticoagulated: current clinic medications (2026-07-10 note) are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily and famotidine, and there is no anticoagulant order in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension (I10/I129), age 65-74, prior ischaemic stroke (2 points) and female sex. Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention in AF.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) documented a home INR of 3.4 and decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under protocol - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist, which the anticoagulation standing order permits and the 2026-03-01 memo covers. A confirmatory INR was therefore required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since the change (the last INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22); the home INR of 3.4 is the trigger, not a completion. The requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation date and is important given her age (95), amiodarone-warfarin interaction and supratherapeutic INR.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 42731) coded 2025-08-22 and carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28. His only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered in clinic. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74, and vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. The coded history of hemorrhage complicating a procedure (99811, 2025-08-22) is a bleeding-risk consideration but not an absolute contraindication, so the gap needs clinician review rather than being assumed intentional.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-07-19 through 2026-06-12 all list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in the problem list (also coded as other specified cardiac dysrhythmias 42789, with Z-code V5861 long-term use of anticoagulants during the June 2025 admission). He received warfarin only as an inpatient (Mar and Jun 2025); his current clinic medications are famotidine and pantoprazole, with no anticoagulant order active. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure (4280 congestive heart failure / 42821 acute systolic heart failure / 4254 cardiomyopathy, Feb 2025) and hypertension (4019). A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any outpatient anticoagulant needs review.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily for atrial flutter (I4892, 2025-09-13). The 2026-08-12 summary-of-episode note records outside records from Mercy Hospital: admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and explicitly states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. No such review is documented, yet the 2026-08-20 cardiology visit lists apixaban 5 mg twice daily as a current medication, says continue current regimen, and a new apixaban order (2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) is active as of the evaluation time, alongside aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) two weeks after a transfusion-requiring upper GI bleed, against an explicit instruction to hold pending review, requires prescriber review.

65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and flutter. The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the anticoagulant is being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban was never stopped: the same visit generated both an apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and a rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25), and the note itself lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily and Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily together in the current medication list. Both orders are still active at the evaluation time, so the patient is on two direct oral anticoagulants simultaneously - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation (he also has a history of rectal haemorrhage, gastrojejunal ulcer, thrombocytopenia and CLL).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day contradict it: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (P-wave prominence 0.11-0.15 mV, beat-to-beat P-window correlation 0.17-0.23) and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 139-144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation (I4891) was in fact coded for that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong and the chart needs correction, since rate control and anticoagulation decisions depend on it.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05, started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology visit). His most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, is sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 519 ms and Bazett QTc 527 ms (RR 0.97 s; tangent-method T offset consistent across leads, 501-535 ms). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug meets the clinic QT monitoring threshold for prescriber review. Electrolytes are not contributory: most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20). He is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

95-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05, continuously prescribed since at least 2022) together with warfarin and metoprolol. Her most recent ECG in the chart, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR 210 ms), QT 539 ms and Bazett QTc 528 ms (RR 1.03 s; per-lead tangent T offsets 490-604 ms, median 539 ms). A most recent ECG with QTc >= 500 ms while on a watch-list medication requires prescriber review under the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14) are within range, so the prolongation is not electrolyte driven. A current ECG has not been obtained in over four years despite continued amiodarone.

interpretations.explanation: 13df78e7 / 2026-03-07. Regular P-QRS-T with upright P in II/III/aVF preceding every QRS (P amplitude 0.31 mV, beat-to-beat P correlation 0.98); RR 658-856 ms with smooth phasic variation = sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia, mean rate 81 bpm. PR 190 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 322 ms at RR 0.74 s giving Bazett QTc 373 ms (per-lead tangent T offsets 311-332 ms). Frontal axis +48 deg (net QRS area lead I +5.7, aVF +3.2) = normal. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms, so no conduction abnormality. This is the only ECG in the chart, obtained 5 days after citalopram was started, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

568cb149 / 2025-07-15. Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02) with a prominent upright P wave before each QRS (P amplitude 0.32 mV). PR 138 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 328 ms at RR 0.58 s giving QTc 431 ms. Axis +33 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Despite his documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both available tracings are sinus. Versus the prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20, sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 395 ms) the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc (+36 ms) show no qualifying change.

5f3dcdb5 / 2024-05-21. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.03) with an upright P before each QRS. PR 122 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 337 ms at RR 0.55 s giving QTc 455 ms (per-lead tangent T offsets very consistent, spread 10 ms) - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold, and he is on no QT watch-list drug. Axis +35 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, normal PR. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

5f74c4bf / 2026-06-10 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 144 bpm: RR intervals 348-650 ms, CV 0.16, half of successive pairs differing by >60 ms, and a completely flat pre-QRS segment with no P waves (P prominence 0.11 mV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.17). No measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 76 ms, QT 281 ms at mean RR 0.42 s giving QTc 435 ms. Axis +5 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening, also showed atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm with QTc 431 ms, so there is no change between them. Note that the clinic note of the same day describes normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which both tracings contradict (raised separately as a documentation conflict).

71a27b6b / 2025-08-02. Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with an upright P before each QRS. PR 160 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 400 ms at RR 0.87 s giving QTc 428 ms. Frontal axis -24 deg (lead I +20.3, aVF -9.2) = normal (borderline leftward). No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. The scattered high-frequency deflections are low-amplitude (<0.15 mV) muscle/mains artefact occurring at the R-peak, not pacing spikes, and there is no evidence of a paced rhythm. Versus the prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus 60 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 399 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or qualifying QTc change (+29 ms).

735c5ea5 / 2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02); a discrete P wave, upright in II, III and aVF (0.33 mV) precedes every QRS at a fixed interval. PR 120 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 298 ms at RR 0.62 s giving QTc 379 ms. Axis +5 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

752d15e2 / 2025-12-25. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with a consistent upright P before each QRS. PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 368 ms at RR 0.83 s giving QTc 404 ms. Axis +22 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, PR normal. This tracing predates the escitalopram start of 2026-08-01, and no ECG has been obtained since; it is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

76202c51 / 2024-11-15. Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53 bpm: RR intervals 696-1164 ms (CV 0.20, 62% of successive pairs differing by >60 ms), no organised P waves (P prominence only 0.05 mV, beat-to-beat P-window correlation -0.10) and a fibrillatory baseline. No measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 76 ms, QT 456 ms at mean RR 1.13 s giving QTc 429 ms. Axis +27 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12, three days earlier) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear 0.39 mV P wave, PR 178 ms and QTc 398 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing (NEW_AF); the QTc change (+31 ms) is not significant.

7ec7078a / 2025-03-09. Sinus rhythm at 58 bpm (mild bradycardia), regular (RR CV 0.03) with a prominent upright P before each QRS (0.37 mV, correlation 0.99). PR 114 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT 399 ms at RR 1.03 s giving QTc 393 ms. Axis +62 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Versus the prior ECG 106045460 from the previous day (2025-03-08, sinus 62 bpm, PR 116 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 426 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or qualifying QTc change (-33 ms). This is the baseline against which the ECG now required after her 2026-09-15 haloperidol start should be compared.

807d2a03 / 2025-08-23. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, essentially metronomic (RR CV 0.00) with a consistent upright P before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR 156 ms, QRS 56 ms, QT 332 ms at RR 0.72 s giving QTc 392 ms. Axis +54 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, normal PR. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

8e77dd0b / 2020-06-19. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with a large upright P before each QRS (0.44 mV, correlation 0.96). PR 160 ms, QRS 60 ms, QT 385 ms at RR 0.78 s giving QTc 435 ms. Axis +64 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Compared with the prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02, sinus 75 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 58 ms, QT 454 ms, QTc 506 ms) the QTc has fallen by 71 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

1cf9e585 / 2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm: metronomically regular RR (coefficient of variation 0.00) with a consistent upright P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.98). PR 174 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 272 ms at RR 0.50 s giving QTc 385 ms (V3-V6, where the T waves are largest, cluster at 265-274 ms; the limb-lead values near 400 ms include a U wave and were rejected). Axis +51 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 180 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 391 ms, normal axis) there is no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -6 ms).

94abdf17 / 2025-06-23. Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01), with an upright P wave before every QRS (0.26 mV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.99). The PR interval is prolonged at 218 ms (P onset 174 ms before the QRS, measured against a flat pre-P baseline), i.e. first-degree AV block; every P is conducted, so this is not higher-grade block. QRS 74 ms, QT 396 ms at RR 1.11 s giving QTc 377 ms. Frontal axis +3 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. Versus the prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51 bpm, PR 190 ms, QRS 74 ms, QTc 359 ms) the PR has lengthened further but rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc (+18 ms) show no change from the defined list.

a0bcbbc0 / 2025-09-13. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 152 bpm: RR intervals 290-580 ms (CV 0.19, 52% of successive pairs differing by >60 ms) with no organised atrial activity (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation -0.03). No measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 88 ms, QT 260 ms at mean RR 0.40 s giving QTc 414 ms. Axis -20 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the day before) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a single early beat, PR 154 ms and QTc 410 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); QTc is unchanged. This matches the unspecified atrial fibrillation coded for the 2025-09-11 admission.

a6e7e991 / 2025-11-23. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild phasic variation (RR 790-924 ms) and a prominent upright P before every QRS (0.36 mV, correlation 0.99). PR 172 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 347 ms at RR 0.82 s giving QTc 384 ms. Axis +13 deg, normal. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. This confirms the clinic note of the same date recording sinus rhythm. Versus the prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus 67 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 500 ms, QTc 529 ms) the QTc has fallen by 145 ms, giving QTC_DECREASE_60; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

aeda7084 / 2025-02-15. Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01), with an upright P before each QRS (0.28 mV, correlation 0.89). PR 190 ms - upper normal but below the 200 ms cut-off, so no first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms, QT 371 ms at RR 0.81 s giving QTc 412 ms. Axis +59 deg, normal. The recording contains scattered narrow high-frequency deflections (~0.3 mV, 70-230 Hz band) that are not time-locked to the QRS complexes; these are artefact rather than pacemaker spikes, and there is no pacemaker in her history, so the rhythm is not paced. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

b410dd44 / 2023-06-26. Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm: RR is essentially fixed (CV 0.00) and a discrete upright P wave precedes each QRS at a constant interval (P 0.25 mV, correlation 0.91); atrial activity shows no 2:1 periodicity, so despite his history of atrial flutter this is sinus, not flutter with fixed conduction. PR 162 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 281 ms at RR 0.54 s giving QTc 383 ms (taken from V1/V2 where the T waves are largest and best defined; limb-lead tangents fell on a following U wave). Axis +34 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Versus the prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 174 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 382 ms) nothing has changed.

b9a9ae7b / 2025-03-14. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early beat (RR sequence 964, 986, 560, 1366, 978, 968, 956, 960, 980 ms - a single premature complex with a compensatory pause; the underlying rhythm is regular and each QRS is preceded by a consistent upright P wave, correlation 0.79), so this is sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat rather than atrial fibrillation. PR is prolonged at 206 ms with a broad P wave, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 90 ms, QT 355 ms at RR 0.97 s giving QTc 361 ms. Frontal axis -32 deg (net QRS area lead I +12.6, aVF -8.0) = left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded at this same admission but is not captured on this tracing.

bbad4581 / 2026-04-29. Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02) with a P wave preceding every QRS at a fixed interval. PR 146 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 351 ms at RR 0.87 s giving QTc 378 ms (per-lead tangent T offsets very consistent, spread 7 ms). Frontal axis -173 deg (net QRS area lead I -18.6, aVF -2.4, with positive aVR) = extreme axis deviation; the globally negative P-QRS-T in leads I and II with a positive aVR raises the possibility of left/right arm lead reversal, which should be considered before treating this as true extreme axis deviation. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; it was obtained 19 days after escitalopram was started and shows no QT prolongation.

bc2a74ce / 2023-11-10. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.03), with an upright P before each QRS (P 0.16 mV, correlation 0.83). PR 158 ms, QRS 86 ms. QT is markedly prolonged at 494 ms with RR 0.86 s, giving Bazett QTc 534 ms; the per-lead tangent T offsets are consistent (478-510 ms). Axis +37 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, PR normal. Compared with the prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 288 ms, QTc 427 ms) the QTc has risen by 107 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies. She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily, and this prolonged QTc is raised separately as a QT safety item.

c0d83ad6 / 2026-03-08. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01), with a 0.25 mV upright P before each QRS (correlation 0.98). PR 146 ms, QRS 74 ms. Repolarisation is somewhat late-peaking (T apex about 310 ms after QRS onset) with a low-amplitude terminal tail, but tangent-method T offsets in the leads with the best-defined T waves (I, III, aVL, aVR, V2) give QT 399 ms at RR 0.88 s, i.e. Bazett QTc 425 ms - prolonged-normal but below the 500 ms review threshold. Axis +60 deg, normal. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; it was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started, satisfying the 30-day monitoring requirement.

c4c29979 / 2019-01-13. Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02) with a prominent upright P before each QRS (0.37 mV, correlation 0.94). PR 180 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 384 ms at RR 1.14 s giving QTc 360 ms (consistent T offsets in II, aVF and V3-V6, 371-384 ms). Axis -6 deg, normal. No bundle branch block; PR below 200 ms so no first-degree AV block. Versus the prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, PR 206 ms i.e. borderline first-degree AV block, QRS 82 ms, QTc 383 ms) the PR interval has in fact shortened; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc (-23 ms) show no change from the defined list.

23069939 / 2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with an upright P before every QRS. PR 158 ms, QRS 78 ms. QT is markedly prolonged at 486 ms with RR 0.88 s, giving Bazett QTc 518 ms; per-lead tangent T offsets are tightly clustered (473-500 ms), so the measurement is reliable. Axis +46 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, PR normal. Versus the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QT 316 ms, QTc 352 ms) the QTc has risen by 166 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies. Rhythm and conduction are unchanged. This is his most recent tracing and he is on escitalopram, so the prolongation is flagged separately for QT safety review.

cb70e6ae / 2022-07-13. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 424 ms, CV 0.02) with no discrete sinus P wave; instead the inter-QRS segment contains a repeating atrial deflection whose period is exactly half the RR interval (212 ms, i.e. an atrial rate of about 283/min). Signal-averaged half-cycle correlation in leads II and aVF is 0.99 and 0.98, confirming two identical atrial waves per ventricular beat: atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. There is no measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 72 ms, QT 266 ms at RR 0.42 s giving QTc 408 ms. Axis +1 deg, normal. QRS is narrow with no pacing spikes, so his pacemaker is not capturing on this tracing. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - chaotically irregular RR 380-824 ms (CV 0.24) with absent P waves (prominence 0.06 mV, correlation 0.06) at 110 bpm, QTc 416 ms. The rhythm has therefore organised: RESOLVED_AF and NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER; QTc is unchanged.

dc332fb6 / 2025-05-12. Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR 150 ms, QRS 92 ms - slightly wide but well under 120 ms, with no rSR' in V1 and no broad monophasic R in V6, so no bundle branch block. QT 374 ms at RR 0.73 s giving QTc 438 ms. Axis +33 deg, normal. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Both orders are still active at the evaluation time, so the patient is on two direct oral anticoagulants simultaneously - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation (he also has a history of rectal haemorrhage, gastrojejunal ulcer, thrombocytopenia and CLL).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day contradict it: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (P-wave prominence 0.11-0.15 mV, beat-to-beat P-window correlation 0.17-0.23) and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 139-144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation (I4891) was in fact coded for that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong and the chart needs correction, since rate control and anticoagulation decisions depend on it.

interpretations.explanation: 13df78e7 / 2026-03-07. Regular P-QRS-T with upright P in II/III/aVF preceding every QRS (P amplitude 0.31 mV, beat-to-beat P correlation 0.98); RR 658-856 ms with smooth phasic variation = sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia, mean rate 81 bpm. 1cf9e585 / 2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm: metronomically regular RR (coefficient of variation 0.00) with a consistent upright P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.98). PR 174 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 272 ms at RR 0.50 s giving QTc 385 ms (V3-V6, where the T waves are largest, cluster at 265-274 ms; the limb-lead values near 400 ms include a U wave and were rejected). Axis +51 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 180 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 391 ms, normal axis) there is no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -6 ms).

23069939 / 2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with an upright P before every QRS. PR 158 ms, QRS 78 ms. QT is markedly prolonged at 486 ms with RR 0.88 s, giving Bazett QTc 518 ms; per-lead tangent T offsets are tightly clustered (473-500 ms), so the measurement is reliable. Axis +46 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, PR normal. Versus the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QT 316 ms, QTc 352 ms) the QTc has risen by 166 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies. Rhythm and conduction are unchanged. This is his most recent tracing and he is on escitalopram, so the prolongation is flagged separately for QT safety review.

28dcf33b / 2024-04-19. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm - perfectly regular RR (CV 0.01) with a discrete upright P before each QRS (P correlation 0.88). PR 142 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 282 ms at RR 0.50 s giving QTc 399 ms (leads with the best-defined T waves, V4-V6 and I/aVR, cluster 272-289 ms). Axis +69 deg, normal. No bundle branch block and normal PR, so no conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2edf1f64 / 2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm, regular with consistent upright P waves (P amplitude 0.35 mV, correlation 0.99). PR 150 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 314 ms at RR 0.59 s giving QTc 409 ms (per-lead spread only 10 ms). Axis +58 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 406 ms), so there are no changes.

3886cafb / 2024-10-24. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm: regular RR (1042 ms, CV 0.01) with an upright P before every QRS (P correlation 0.90). PR 178 ms - prolonged for age but below the 200 ms threshold, so no first-degree AV block is coded despite the chart diagnosis of Mobitz II block; no dropped beats are seen on this 10-second tracing. QRS 82 ms, QT 429 ms at RR 1.15 s giving QTc 398 ms. Axis +36 deg, normal. Versus the prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus bradycardia 57 bpm with a single ectopic beat, PR 156 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 376 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (+22 ms).

arguments.explanation: 4365e125 / 2024-12-05 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular with an upright P before each QRS (P correlation 0.97). PR 134 ms, QRS now only 76 ms with an rSr' in V1 (terminal r' 0.10 mV) and a terminal S in I and V6 - an incomplete right bundle branch block pattern that no longer meets the >=120 ms criterion, so no complete RBBB is coded. QT 285 ms at RR 0.50 s giving QTc 406 ms. Frontal axis +141 deg (net QRS area lead I -1.1, aVF +0.9) = right axis deviation. The prior tracing 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) showed complete RBBB: QRS 138 ms with rSR' in V1 (R' peak 1.13 mV, 108 ms after QRS onset) and a broad terminal S in I/V6, QT 363 ms, QTc 469 ms. The bundle branch block has therefore resolved (rate-related RBBB), and with loss of the 60 ms of terminal QRS the QTc fell by 63 ms, meeting QTC_DECREASE_60.

5f74c4bf / 2026-06-10 19:36. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 180 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 391 ms, normal axis) there is no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -6 ms).

No bundle branch block, PR normal. Versus the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QT 316 ms, QTc 352 ms) the QTc has risen by 166 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies. Rhythm and conduction are unchanged. This is his most recent tracing and he is on escitalopram, so the prolongation is flagged separately for QT safety review.

No bundle branch block and normal PR, so no conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2edf1f64 / 2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm, regular with consistent upright P waves (P amplitude 0.35 mV, correlation 0.99). Versus the prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus bradycardia 57 bpm with a single ectopic beat, PR 156 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 376 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (+22 ms).

4365e125 / 2024-12-05 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular with an upright P before each QRS (P correlation 0.97). QT 285 ms at RR 0.50 s giving QTc 406 ms. Frontal axis +141 deg (net QRS area lead I -1.1, aVF +0.9) = right axis deviation. The prior tracing 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) showed complete RBBB: QRS 138 ms with rSR' in V1 (R' peak 1.13 mV, 108 ms after QRS onset) and a broad terminal S in I/V6, QT 363 ms, QTc 469 ms. The bundle branch block has therefore resolved (rate-related RBBB), and with loss of the 60 ms of terminal QRS the QTc fell by 63 ms, meeting QTC_DECREASE_60.

4c48ec6f / 2025-11-24. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01), upright P before every QRS (P correlation 0.93). PR 176 ms, QRS 86 ms. QT is markedly prolonged at 519 ms with RR 0.97 s, giving Bazett QTc 527 ms; per-lead tangent T offsets agree closely (501-535 ms across ten leads). Axis +66 deg, normal. No bundle branch block; PR <200 ms so no first-degree AV block. Compared with the prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, PR 188 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 461 ms, QTc 409 ms) the QTc has increased by 118 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60 - coinciding with amiodarone having been started on 2025-11-10. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

51d2190c / 2024-09-17. arguments.explanation: 71a27b6b / 2025-08-02. Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with an upright P before each QRS. PR 160 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 400 ms at RR 0.87 s giving QTc 428 ms. No INR has been resulted since the change (the last INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22); the home INR of 3.4 is the trigger, not a completion. The requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation date and is important given her age (95), amiodarone-warfarin interaction and supratherapeutic INR.

A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any outpatient anticoagulant needs review.

The 2026-08-12 summary-of-episode note records outside records from Mercy Hospital: admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and explicitly states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) two weeks after a transfusion-requiring upper GI bleed, against an explicit instruction to hold pending review, requires prescriber review.

The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the anticoagulant is being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban was never stopped: the same visit generated both an apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and a rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25), and the note itself lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily and Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily together in the current medication list. Both orders are still active at the evaluation time, so the patient is on two direct oral anticoagulants simultaneously - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation (he also has a history of rectal haemorrhage, gastrojejunal ulcer, thrombocytopenia and CLL).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day contradict it: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (P-wave prominence 0.11-0.15 mV, beat-to-beat P-window correlation 0.17-0.23) and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 139-144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation (I4891) was in fact coded for that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong and the chart needs correction, since rate control and anticoagulation decisions depend on it.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 2025-09-12, 2026-03-12, 2026-05-28). Current medications at the 2026-05-28 visit are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only; the only anticoagulants in the chart are inpatient dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban orders from January 2025, none of them current. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: CHF (I5040/I110 congestive heart failure, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure), hypertension (I10), age 80 (2 points), type 2 diabetes (E119/E11649), prior TIA/cerebral infarction (V1254, I69322/I69351) (2 points), vascular disease (old MI 412, coronary atherosclerosis I2510) and female sex. Guideline-indicated oral anticoagulation is absent; antiplatelet therapy alone is not an acceptable substitute.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25, continuously prescribed since at least 2023). Her most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, QRS 86 ms, QT 494 ms and Bazett QTc 534 ms (RR 0.86 s; per-lead tangent T offsets tightly clustered 478-510 ms). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review under the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. In addition, 40 mg daily exceeds the maximum recommended citalopram dose and she has hypothyroidism and prior acute kidney failure, all of which add to the torsade risk; dose reduction and a repeat ECG should be considered.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02, continuous since it was started at the 2024-05-14 cardiology visit). His most recent ECG in the chart, 108018814 of 2023-10-08, shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 486 ms and Bazett QTc 518 ms (RR 0.88 s; per-lead tangent T offsets clustered 473-500 ms). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list medication requires prescriber review. Note that the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same 2023-10-08 ECG as sinus rhythm, QT acceptable, which the measured QTc does not support. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2025-08-23) are normal, and no ECG has been repeated since starting the drug.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10. Because the start date is before 2026-03-01, the 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (The ECG itself showed QTc 527 ms, which is handled as a separate QT_SAFETY item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start predates 2026-03-01, so the original 2025-09-01 memo window of 30 days applies (the 2026-03-01 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day window), giving a due date of 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - within the 30-day window, so completed. The ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc 425 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on or after 2026-03-01, the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded 2026-03-07, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc 373 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo applies: ECG required within 14 days, due 2026-04-24. No ECG was obtained inside that window - the only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not satisfied within the required time and is overdue as of the evaluation date. (That late ECG showed sinus rhythm 69 bpm, QTc 378 ms, so no QT safety issue, but the monitoring requirement itself was missed.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the drug was started - and no outside ECG is referenced. The due date has passed, so this monitoring requirement is overdue.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 for her psychotic disorder. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained yet (last ECGs 2025-03-08/09), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked to ensure the ECG is done by 2026-09-29.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10. Start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart for the patient at all, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the 14-day window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained, would satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives; the report should be chased and the QTc reviewed.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was met.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I480) coded at the 2025-03-14 admission, during which she also had a cardioembolic cerebral infarction (I6340 cerebral infarction due to embolism, I69354 residual hemiplegia). She has never been anticoagulated: current clinic medications (2026-07-10 note) are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily and famotidine, and there is no anticoagulant order in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension (I10/I129), age 65-74, prior ischaemic stroke (2 points) and female sex. Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention in AF.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) documented a home INR of 3.4 and decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under protocol - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist, which the anticoagulation standing order permits and the 2026-03-01 memo covers. A confirmatory INR was therefore required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since the change (the last INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22); the home INR of 3.4 is the trigger, not a completion. The requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation date and is important given her age (95), amiodarone-warfarin interaction and supratherapeutic INR.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 42731) coded 2025-08-22 and carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28. His only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered in clinic. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74, and vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. The coded history of hemorrhage complicating a procedure (99811, 2025-08-22) is a bleeding-risk consideration but not an absolute contraindication, so the gap needs clinician review rather than being assumed intentional.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-07-19 through 2026-06-12 all list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in the problem list (also coded as other specified cardiac dysrhythmias 42789, with Z-code V5861 long-term use of anticoagulants during the June 2025 admission). He received warfarin only as an inpatient (Mar and Jun 2025); his current clinic medications are famotidine and pantoprazole, with no anticoagulant order active. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure (4280 congestive heart failure / 42821 acute systolic heart failure / 4254 cardiomyopathy, Feb 2025) and hypertension (4019). A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any outpatient anticoagulant needs review.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily for atrial flutter (I4892, 2025-09-13). The 2026-08-12 summary-of-episode note records outside records from Mercy Hospital: admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and explicitly states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. No such review is documented, yet the 2026-08-20 cardiology visit lists apixaban 5 mg twice daily as a current medication, says continue current regimen, and a new apixaban order (2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) is active as of the evaluation time, alongside aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) two weeks after a transfusion-requiring upper GI bleed, against an explicit instruction to hold pending review, requires prescriber review.

65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and flutter. The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the anticoagulant is being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban was never stopped: the same visit generated both an apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and a rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25), and the note itself lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily and Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily together in the current medication list. Both orders are still active at the evaluation time, so the patient is on two direct oral anticoagulants simultaneously - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation (he also has a history of rectal haemorrhage, gastrojejunal ulcer, thrombocytopenia and CLL).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day contradict it: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (P-wave prominence 0.11-0.15 mV, beat-to-beat P-window correlation 0.17-0.23) and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 139-144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation (I4891) was in fact coded for that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong and the chart needs correction, since rate control and anticoagulation decisions depend on it.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05, started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology visit). His most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, is sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 519 ms and Bazett QTc 527 ms (RR 0.97 s; tangent-method T offset consistent across leads, 501-535 ms). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug meets the clinic QT monitoring threshold for prescriber review. Electrolytes are not contributory: most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20). He is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

95-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05, continuously prescribed since at least 2022) together with warfarin and metoprolol. Her most recent ECG in the chart, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR 210 ms), QT 539 ms and Bazett QTc 528 ms (RR 1.03 s; per-lead tangent T offsets 490-604 ms, median 539 ms). A most recent ECG with QTc >= 500 ms while on a watch-list medication requires prescriber review under the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14) are within range, so the prolongation is not electrolyte driven. A current ECG has not been obtained in over four years despite continued amiodarone.

interpretations.explanation: 13df78e7 / 2026-03-07. Regular P-QRS-T with upright P in II/III/aVF preceding every QRS (P amplitude 0.31 mV, beat-to-beat P correlation 0.98); RR 658-856 ms with smooth phasic variation = sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia, mean rate 81 bpm. PR 190 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 322 ms at RR 0.74 s giving Bazett QTc 373 ms (per-lead tangent T offsets 311-332 ms). Frontal axis +48 deg (net QRS area lead I +5.7, aVF +3.2) = normal. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms, so no conduction abnormality. This is the only ECG in the chart, obtained 5 days after citalopram was started, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

568cb149 / 2025-07-15. Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02) with a prominent upright P wave before each QRS (P amplitude 0.32 mV). PR 138 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 328 ms at RR 0.58 s giving QTc 431 ms. Axis +33 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Despite his documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both available tracings are sinus. Versus the prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20, sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 395 ms) the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc (+36 ms) show no qualifying change.

5f3dcdb5 / 2024-05-21. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.03) with an upright P before each QRS. PR 122 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 337 ms at RR 0.55 s giving QTc 455 ms (per-lead tangent T offsets very consistent, spread 10 ms) - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold, and he is on no QT watch-list drug. Axis +35 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, normal PR. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

5f74c4bf / 2026-06-10 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 144 bpm: RR intervals 348-650 ms, CV 0.16, half of successive pairs differing by >60 ms, and a completely flat pre-QRS segment with no P waves (P prominence 0.11 mV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.17). No measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 76 ms, QT 281 ms at mean RR 0.42 s giving QTc 435 ms. Axis +5 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening, also showed atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm with QTc 431 ms, so there is no change between them. Note that the clinic note of the same day describes normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which both tracings contradict (raised separately as a documentation conflict).

71a27b6b / 2025-08-02. Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with an upright P before each QRS. PR 160 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 400 ms at RR 0.87 s giving QTc 428 ms. Frontal axis -24 deg (lead I +20.3, aVF -9.2) = normal (borderline leftward). No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. The scattered high-frequency deflections are low-amplitude (<0.15 mV) muscle/mains artefact occurring at the R-peak, not pacing spikes, and there is no evidence of a paced rhythm. Versus the prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus 60 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 399 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or qualifying QTc change (+29 ms).

735c5ea5 / 2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02); a discrete P wave, upright in II, III and aVF (0.33 mV) precedes every QRS at a fixed interval. PR 120 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 298 ms at RR 0.62 s giving QTc 379 ms. Axis +5 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

752d15e2 / 2025-12-25. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with a consistent upright P before each QRS. PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 368 ms at RR 0.83 s giving QTc 404 ms. Axis +22 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, PR normal. This tracing predates the escitalopram start of 2026-08-01, and no ECG has been obtained since; it is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

76202c51 / 2024-11-15. Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53 bpm: RR intervals 696-1164 ms (CV 0.20, 62% of successive pairs differing by >60 ms), no organised P waves (P prominence only 0.05 mV, beat-to-beat P-window correlation -0.10) and a fibrillatory baseline. No measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 76 ms, QT 456 ms at mean RR 1.13 s giving QTc 429 ms. Axis +27 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12, three days earlier) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear 0.39 mV P wave, PR 178 ms and QTc 398 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing (NEW_AF); the QTc change (+31 ms) is not significant.

7ec7078a / 2025-03-09. Sinus rhythm at 58 bpm (mild bradycardia), regular (RR CV 0.03) with a prominent upright P before each QRS (0.37 mV, correlation 0.99). PR 114 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT 399 ms at RR 1.03 s giving QTc 393 ms. Axis +62 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Versus the prior ECG 106045460 from the previous day (2025-03-08, sinus 62 bpm, PR 116 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 426 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or qualifying QTc change (-33 ms). This is the baseline against which the ECG now required after her 2026-09-15 haloperidol start should be compared.

807d2a03 / 2025-08-23. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, essentially metronomic (RR CV 0.00) with a consistent upright P before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR 156 ms, QRS 56 ms, QT 332 ms at RR 0.72 s giving QTc 392 ms. Axis +54 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, normal PR. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

8e77dd0b / 2020-06-19. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with a large upright P before each QRS (0.44 mV, correlation 0.96). PR 160 ms, QRS 60 ms, QT 385 ms at RR 0.78 s giving QTc 435 ms. Axis +64 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Compared with the prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02, sinus 75 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 58 ms, QT 454 ms, QTc 506 ms) the QTc has fallen by 71 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

1cf9e585 / 2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm: metronomically regular RR (coefficient of variation 0.00) with a consistent upright P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.98). PR 174 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 272 ms at RR 0.50 s giving QTc 385 ms (V3-V6, where the T waves are largest, cluster at 265-274 ms; the limb-lead values near 400 ms include a U wave and were rejected). Axis +51 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 180 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 391 ms, normal axis) there is no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -6 ms).

94abdf17 / 2025-06-23. Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01), with an upright P wave before every QRS (0.26 mV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.99). The PR interval is prolonged at 218 ms (P onset 174 ms before the QRS, measured against a flat pre-P baseline), i.e. first-degree AV block; every P is conducted, so this is not higher-grade block. QRS 74 ms, QT 396 ms at RR 1.11 s giving QTc 377 ms. Frontal axis +3 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. Versus the prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51 bpm, PR 190 ms, QRS 74 ms, QTc 359 ms) the PR has lengthened further but rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc (+18 ms) show no change from the defined list.

a0bcbbc0 / 2025-09-13. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 152 bpm: RR intervals 290-580 ms (CV 0.19, 52% of successive pairs differing by >60 ms) with no organised atrial activity (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation -0.03). No measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 88 ms, QT 260 ms at mean RR 0.40 s giving QTc 414 ms. Axis -20 deg, normal. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the day before) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a single early beat, PR 154 ms and QTc 410 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); QTc is unchanged. This matches the unspecified atrial fibrillation coded for the 2025-09-11 admission.

a6e7e991 / 2025-11-23. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild phasic variation (RR 790-924 ms) and a prominent upright P before every QRS (0.36 mV, correlation 0.99). PR 172 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 347 ms at RR 0.82 s giving QTc 384 ms. Axis +13 deg, normal. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. This confirms the clinic note of the same date recording sinus rhythm. Versus the prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus 67 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 500 ms, QTc 529 ms) the QTc has fallen by 145 ms, giving QTC_DECREASE_60; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

aeda7084 / 2025-02-15. Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01), with an upright P before each QRS (0.28 mV, correlation 0.89). PR 190 ms - upper normal but below the 200 ms cut-off, so no first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms, QT 371 ms at RR 0.81 s giving QTc 412 ms. Axis +59 deg, normal. The recording contains scattered narrow high-frequency deflections (~0.3 mV, 70-230 Hz band) that are not time-locked to the QRS complexes; these are artefact rather than pacemaker spikes, and there is no pacemaker in her history, so the rhythm is not paced. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

b410dd44 / 2023-06-26. Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm: RR is essentially fixed (CV 0.00) and a discrete upright P wave precedes each QRS at a constant interval (P 0.25 mV, correlation 0.91); atrial activity shows no 2:1 periodicity, so despite his history of atrial flutter this is sinus, not flutter with fixed conduction. PR 162 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 281 ms at RR 0.54 s giving QTc 383 ms (taken from V1/V2 where the T waves are largest and best defined; limb-lead tangents fell on a following U wave). Axis +34 deg, normal. No conduction abnormality. Versus the prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 174 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 382 ms) nothing has changed.

b9a9ae7b / 2025-03-14. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early beat (RR sequence 964, 986, 560, 1366, 978, 968, 956, 960, 980 ms - a single premature complex with a compensatory pause; the underlying rhythm is regular and each QRS is preceded by a consistent upright P wave, correlation 0.79), so this is sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat rather than atrial fibrillation. PR is prolonged at 206 ms with a broad P wave, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 90 ms, QT 355 ms at RR 0.97 s giving QTc 361 ms. Frontal axis -32 deg (net QRS area lead I +12.6, aVF -8.0) = left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded at this same admission but is not captured on this tracing.

bbad4581 / 2026-04-29. Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02) with a P wave preceding every QRS at a fixed interval. PR 146 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 351 ms at RR 0.87 s giving QTc 378 ms (per-lead tangent T offsets very consistent, spread 7 ms). Frontal axis -173 deg (net QRS area lead I -18.6, aVF -2.4, with positive aVR) = extreme axis deviation; the globally negative P-QRS-T in leads I and II with a positive aVR raises the possibility of left/right arm lead reversal, which should be considered before treating this as true extreme axis deviation. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; it was obtained 19 days after escitalopram was started and shows no QT prolongation.

bc2a74ce / 2023-11-10. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.03), with an upright P before each QRS (P 0.16 mV, correlation 0.83). PR 158 ms, QRS 86 ms. QT is markedly prolonged at 494 ms with RR 0.86 s, giving Bazett QTc 534 ms; the per-lead tangent T offsets are consistent (478-510 ms). Axis +37 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, PR normal. Compared with the prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 288 ms, QTc 427 ms) the QTc has risen by 107 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies. She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily, and this prolonged QTc is raised separately as a QT safety item.

c0d83ad6 / 2026-03-08. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01), with a 0.25 mV upright P before each QRS (correlation 0.98). PR 146 ms, QRS 74 ms. Repolarisation is somewhat late-peaking (T apex about 310 ms after QRS onset) with a low-amplitude terminal tail, but tangent-method T offsets in the leads with the best-defined T waves (I, III, aVL, aVR, V2) give QT 399 ms at RR 0.88 s, i.e. Bazett QTc 425 ms - prolonged-normal but below the 500 ms review threshold. Axis +60 deg, normal. No bundle branch block and PR <200 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; it was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started, satisfying the 30-day monitoring requirement.

c4c29979 / 2019-01-13. Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.02) with a prominent upright P before each QRS (0.37 mV, correlation 0.94). PR 180 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 384 ms at RR 1.14 s giving QTc 360 ms (consistent T offsets in II, aVF and V3-V6, 371-384 ms). Axis -6 deg, normal. No bundle branch block; PR below 200 ms so no first-degree AV block. Versus the prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, PR 206 ms i.e. borderline first-degree AV block, QRS 82 ms, QTc 383 ms) the PR interval has in fact shortened; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc (-23 ms) show no change from the defined list.

23069939 / 2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with an upright P before every QRS. PR 158 ms, QRS 78 ms. QT is markedly prolonged at 486 ms with RR 0.88 s, giving Bazett QTc 518 ms; per-lead tangent T offsets are tightly clustered (473-500 ms), so the measurement is reliable. Axis +46 deg, normal. No bundle branch block, PR normal. Versus the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QT 316 ms, QTc 352 ms) the QTc has risen by 166 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies. Rhythm and conduction are unchanged. This is his most recent tracing and he is on escitalopram, so the prolongation is flagged separately for QT safety review.

cb70e6ae / 2022-07-13. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 424 ms, CV 0.02) with no discrete sinus P wave; instead the inter-QRS segment contains a repeating atrial deflection whose period is exactly half the RR interval (212 ms, i.e. an atrial rate of about 283/min). Signal-averaged half-cycle correlation in leads II and aVF is 0.99 and 0.98, confirming two identical atrial waves per ventricular beat: atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. There is no measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS 72 ms, QT 266 ms at RR 0.42 s giving QTc 408 ms. Axis +1 deg, normal. QRS is narrow with no pacing spikes, so his pacemaker is not capturing on this tracing. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - chaotically irregular RR 380-824 ms (CV 0.24) with absent P waves (prominence 0.06 mV, correlation 0.06) at 110 bpm, QTc 416 ms. The rhythm has therefore organised: RESOLVED_AF and NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER; QTc is unchanged.

dc332fb6 / 2025-05-12. Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR CV 0.01) with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any outpatient anticoagulant needs review.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily for atrial flutter (I4892, 2025-09-13). The 2026-08-12 summary-of-episode note records outside records from Mercy Hospital: admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and explicitly states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) two weeks after a transfusion-requiring upper GI bleed, against an explicit instruction to hold pending review, requires prescriber review.

65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and flutter. The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the anticoagulant is being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban was never stopped: the same visit generated both an apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and a rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25), and the note itself lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily and Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily together in the current medication list. Both orders are still active at the evaluation time, so the patient is on two direct oral anticoagulants simultaneously - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation (he also has a history of rectal haemorrhage, gastrojejunal ulcer, thrombocytopenia and CLL).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day contradict it: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (P-wave prominence 0.11-0.15 mV, beat-to-beat P-window correlation 0.17-0.23) and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 139-144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation (I4891) was in fact coded for that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong and the chart needs correction, since rate control and anticoagulation decisions depend on it.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list; current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05, started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology visit). Electrolytes are not contributory: most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20). He is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14) are within range, so the prolongation is not electrolyte driven. A current ECG has not been obtained in over four years despite continued amiodarone.
